docs.summary: Central undo/redo system for the editor. Supports property changes (via Echo serialization), structural changes (create/delete GO), and generic action-based undo via lambdas.

members.name: MaxSteps
members.signature: public static int MaxSteps { get; set; }

docs.summary: Maximum number of undo steps kept in the undo stack. Defaults to 100.
Fires after an undo or redo operation completes.
Description of the next undo operation, or "Undo" if the stack is empty.
Description of the next redo operation, or "Redo" if the stack is empty.

Snapshot an object's current state for undo. Call at the TOP of PropertyGrid.Draw() or custom editor OnGUI(), BEFORE any widgets draw this captures the state before any in-place mutations (nested objects, collections, curves, etc.). No-op if already snapshotted this frame for the same target.

members.name: RegisterAction
members.signature: public static void RegisterAction(string description, Action undo, Action redo)

docs.summary: Register an undoable action with explicit undo/redo lambdas.

members.name: RecordGameObjectChange
members.signature: public static void RecordGameObjectChange<T>(GameObject go, string description, T oldValue, T newValue, Action<GameObject, T> apply, bool coalesce = false)

docs.summary: Records a property change on a GameObject, looking the GO back up by Identifier on undo/redo so the record survives destroy/recreate cycles. Apply receives the live GO and the value to assign. Caller is still responsible for the immediate write - this only registers the undo entry.

members.name: RegisterCoalescableAction
members.signature: public static void RegisterCoalescableAction(string description, Action undo, Action redo)

docs.summary: Register an undoable action that coalesces with the previous action if it has the same description and is within the time window. Use for continuous text input (Name fields, etc.). The undo lambda is kept from the FIRST action; the redo lambda is updated to the LATEST.

members.name: RegisterActionGroup
members.signature: public static void RegisterActionGroup(string description, IReadOnlyList<(Action undo, Action redo)> actions, bool coalesce = false)

docs.summary: Register several undo/redo actions as ONE undo step (so editing many selected objects in a single interaction collapses to a single undo). When `coalesce` is true the step merges with the previous step if it has the same description and record count within the coalesce window (for continuous edits like dragging a multi-object transform field).

members.name: ApplyGameObjectChanges
members.signature: public static void ApplyGameObjectChanges<T>(IReadOnlyList<GameObject> gos, string description, Func<GameObject, T> get, Action<GameObject, T> set, T newValue, bool coalesce = false)

docs.summary: Apply a value to every given GameObject and record the change as a single grouped undo step. Captures each object's current value as the undo state, then writes the new value. Mirrors [`RecordGameObjectChange`](#api~Prowl.Editor.Core.Undo~RecordGameObjectChange) but batched across a multi-object selection.

members.name: RegisterCreatedObject
members.signature: public static void RegisterCreatedObject(GameObject go, string description)

docs.summary: Register that a GameObject was just created. Undo will destroy it, redo will recreate it. Serialization is deferred to FlushFrame so components added after this call are captured. Call AFTER the GO has been added to the scene and parented.

members.name: CaptureCreatedObject
members.signature: public static (Action undo, Action redo) CaptureCreatedObject(GameObject go)

docs.summary: Build the undo/redo pair for a just-created GameObject without pushing it as its own step, so a compound operation can hand it to [`RegisterActionGroup`](#api~Prowl.Editor.Core.Undo~RegisterActionGroup) together with the follow-up actions that depend on it (e.g. "Create Empty Parent" = new object + reparenting). Splitting those across two steps would let the object be destroyed while the objects moved under it still live there, taking them down with it. Unlike [`RegisterCreatedObject`](#api~Prowl.Editor.Core.Undo~RegisterCreatedObject) this serializes immediately, so call it while the object is still in the state redo should restore it to - before the follow-up actions run.

members.name: RegisterDestroyObject
members.signature: public static void RegisterDestroyObject(GameObject go, string description)

docs.summary: Register that a GameObject is about to be destroyed. Undo will recreate it, redo will destroy it. Call BEFORE the GO is removed from the scene.

members.name: BeginContinuous
members.signature: public static void BeginContinuous(GameObject[] targets, string description)

docs.summary: Begin a continuous undo operation (e.g., gizmo drag). Snapshots all targets' transforms at the start. Call EndContinuous when done.
End a continuous operation and push one undo step if anything changed.
Cancel a continuous operation without pushing an undo step. Restores all targets to their start state.
Force a new group boundary. Flushes any pending records into a step, so the next RecordObject starts a fresh step.
Perform one undo step. If a continuous operation is active, cancels it instead. Flushes pending records before undoing.
Perform one redo step. Does nothing if a continuous operation is active. Flushes pending records before redoing.
Clear all undo/redo history. Called on scene load.
Drops edits that were captured but not yet recorded, keeping the undo and redo history.
Find a GameObject by identifier in the current scene. Returns null if not found. Use this in undo/redo lambdas instead of capturing GO references directly.
Find a component by identifier across all GOs in the current scene.
